concepts.def: H0 ~ 70 km/s per Mpc, present expansion rate.
Speed at which a galaxy moves away due to expansion.
Density needed for a flat universe.

walkthroughs.body_html: If a galaxy is 200 Mpc away and H0 = 70 km/s/Mpc, recession speed v = 70 x 200 = 14,000 km/s. Reversing: a galaxy receding at 21,000 km/s sits at 300 Mpc.
For small redshifts, z ~ v/c. So a galaxy with z = 0.01 recedes at ~3000 km/s. Larger z values require relativistic formulas.
1/H0 ~ 14 billion years gives a rough age estimate close to the true 13.8 billion years. This is striking evidence the universe really did begin expanding.
